name: fsa-ch01-introduction
description: Frames software architecture as four interlocking dimensions (characteristics, logical components, style, decisions) analyzed in that order, applies three laws (trade-offs everywhere, rationale over mechanism, decisions on a spectrum) and the eight expectations of an architect. Based on Chapter 1 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when scoping an architecture effort, separating architectural from technical decisions, challenging "no trade-off" claims, checking decision compliance or vitality, or coaching someone growing into the architect role.

name: fsa-ch02-architectural-thinking
description: Applies the architectural-thinking mindset from Chapter 2 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers placing a decision on the architecture-versus-design spectrum, two-sided trade-off analysis, translating business drivers into architecture characteristics, building technical breadth (knowledge pyramid, daily learning habit, personal technology radar), and staying hands-on without becoming a bottleneck. Use when deciding who owns a decision, comparing options, planning an architect's learning, or advising a developer moving into architecture.

name: fsa-ch03-modularity
description: Modularity analysis for architects, based on Chapter 3 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers modularity versus granularity, the cohesion scale, LCOM, afferent/efferent coupling, abstractness, instability, distance from the main sequence (zones of pain and uselessness) and connascence (forms, strength, locality, degree). Use when sizing or splitting modules or services, reviewing coupling, assessing a code base before a migration, measuring technical debt, or naming a coupling problem in a code or design review.

name: fsa-ch04-characteristics-defined
description: Defines what counts as an architecture characteristic, how to tell it apart from domain requirements and ordinary design hygiene, how to categorize and name characteristics (operational, structural, cloud, cross-cutting, ISO families), and why to keep the set small and accept least-worst trade-offs. Based on Chapter 4 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when sorting a requirements list into domain vs. capabilities, deciding whether a concern needs structural support, building a shared glossary of "-ilities", or pruning an overlong list of quality goal…

name: fsa-ch05-identifying-characteristics
description: Guides identification of architecture characteristics ("-ilities") from domain concerns, requirements and implicit domain knowledge; decomposing composite goals like agility; telling scalability from elasticity; deciding architecture versus design; and pruning to a short prioritized list via a worksheet and top-three selection. Based on Chapter 5 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when gathering non-functional requirements, translating business goals into -ilities, running an architecture kata, or running a stakeholder prioritization session.

name: fsa-ch06-measuring-and-governing
description: Turns vague architecture characteristics into objective operational, structural and process measures, and governs them with automated fitness functions (cycle checks, layer rules, main-sequence distance, complexity gates, chaos-style production checks). Based on Chapter 6 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when defining measurable "-ilities", choosing latency or deployability metrics, setting Cyclomatic Complexity thresholds, writing architecture tests for CI, or stopping modularity erosion.

name: fsa-ch07-scope-of-characteristics
description: Scopes architecture characteristics with the architecture quantum (independently deployable, cohesive unit with its data) and uses that scope to pick monolithic vs distributed styles, draw service boundaries, choose persistence and sync vs async communication, and scope cloud-hosted parts. Based on Chapter 7 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed). Use when deciding whether one set of characteristics fits the whole system, finding quanta, spotting shared-database or shared-library coupling, or diagnosing failing calls between services with mismatched scalabilit…

name: fsa-ch08-component-based-thinking
description: Guides identifying, sizing and refining logical components and analyzing coupling between them, based on Chapter 8 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when drawing a logical architecture before a physical one, seeding components with the Workflow or Actor/Action approach, spotting Entity Trap "Manager" components, assigning user stories, splitting components for cohesion or architecture characteristics, computing afferent/efferent coupling, finding temporal coupling, or applying the Law of Demeter.

name: fsa-ch09-style-foundations
description: Foundational decision rules for architecture styles, based on Chapter 9 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers style versus pattern, Big Ball of Mud, client/server and three-tier lineage, technical versus domain top-level partitioning, Conway's Law, monolithic versus distributed, the eleven fallacies of distributed computing, and team topologies. Use when choosing monolith versus distributed, deciding how to partition components, reviewing a plan to split a system into services, or estimating latency, availability and bandwidth of remote call chains.

name: fsa-ch10-layered-style
description: Guidance for evaluating, designing and governing the layered (n-tier) architecture style, based on Chapter 10 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers logical and physical layer topology, open vs closed layers, layers of isolation, the Architecture Sinkhole 80/20 check, cloud, risk, governance and team fit. Use when choosing or rejecting a layered monolith, reviewing layer dependencies, deciding which layers may be skipped, writing layer fitness functions, or diagnosing a layered system that is outgrowing itself.

name: fsa-ch11-modular-monolith
description: Guidance for evaluating, designing and governing a modular monolith (one deployable, code partitioned by business domain), based on Chapter 11 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers single-repo vs per-module artifacts, peer-to-peer vs mediator communication, data topology, risks, fitness functions and team alignment. Use when choosing a starting architecture, restructuring a layered monolith by domain, reviewing module boundaries, writing boundary checks, or deciding when a monolith has outgrown itself.

name: fsa-ch12-pipeline-style
description: Guidance for evaluating, designing and governing the pipeline (pipes and filters) architecture style, based on Chapter 12 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers filter roles (producer, transformer, tester, consumer), pipe contracts, data and cloud topologies, risks, tag-based governance, team fit and trade-offs. Use when a user designs ETL, EDI, telemetry or step-by-step workflows, asks whether pipes and filters fits, reviews an overloaded or bidirectional pipeline, or weighs monolithic versus distributed filters.

name: fsa-ch13-microkernel-style
description: Guides evaluation, design and governance of the microkernel (plug-in) architecture style: stable core vs volatile plug-ins, registries, contracts, data ownership, remote plug-ins, cloud placement, risks, fitness functions and team split. Based on Chapter 13 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when a system needs per-client, per-jurisdiction or per-product customization, when deciding whether a plug-in design is appropriate, when designing a core/plug-in boundary, or when reviewing an existing plug-in system for drift.

name: fsa-ch14-service-based-style
description: Applies the service-based architecture style (coarse-grained domain services, optional shared database) from Chapter 14 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when evaluating whether a system should be service-based versus monolithic or microservices, designing domain services, UIs, gateways or database topology, managing shared-database schema change, governing service count and coupling, aligning teams, or planning a stepping-stone migration toward microservices.

name: fsa-ch15-event-driven-style
description: Guidance on the event-driven architecture style based on Chapter 15 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers events vs messages, derived and extensible events, payload design (data-based vs key-based, anemic events, Swarm of Gnats), error handling, data-loss prevention, request-reply, mediator vs choreography, data topologies, risks, governance and team fit. Use when deciding whether EDA fits, designing or reviewing event flows and contracts, choosing a mediator or database topology, or writing fitness functions for an event-driven system.

name: fsa-ch16-space-based-style
description: Guidance for evaluating, designing and governing space-based architectures (processing units, replicated in-memory data grids, data pumps, readers and writers, elastic deployment), based on Chapter 16 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture". Use when a system faces extreme or spiky concurrency, when choosing replicated versus distributed caching, estimating data-collision risk, planning cache-to-database sync, defining fitness functions for memory and sync time, aligning teams, or deciding whether the style is worth its cost and complexity.

name: fsa-ch17-orchestration-driven-soa
description: Guidance on orchestration-driven service-oriented architecture (SOA) and its modern legacy, based on Chapter 17 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture". Covers the layered service taxonomy, orchestration engines and ESBs, reuse-versus-coupling trade-offs, canonical entity pitfalls, single-quantum characteristics, the Accidental SOA antipattern, and fitness functions for integration hubs. Use when evaluating an ESB or central workflow engine, reviewing shared "canonical" services, diagnosing slow cross-layer change, or designing legacy-to-modern integration.

name: fsa-ch18-microservices
description: Applies the microservices architecture style as described in Chapter 18 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Covers bounded-context boundaries, service granularity, data isolation and database topologies, API layer limits, sidecars and service mesh, choreography vs orchestration, sagas, governance of coupling, team topologies, and fit. Use when deciding whether microservices suits a system, sizing or splitting services, choosing a data topology, reviewing a microservices design for risks, or setting up coupling governance.

name: fsa-ch19-choosing-a-style
description: Guides selection of an architecture style (monolith vs distributed, layered, modular monolith, microkernel, microservices, event-driven, space-based, service-based) from domain knowledge, architecture characteristics, data, cloud, organizational and team factors, and domain/architecture shape fit. Based on Chapter 19 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.). Use when asked which architecture style to pick, whether to split a system, where data should live, sync vs async between services, or how to judge an industry architecture trend.

name: fsa-ch20-architectural-patterns
description: Applies Chapter 20 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.) on architectural patterns as contextual solutions distinct from styles, best practices and tools. Use when choosing or naming a pattern, standardizing cross-cutting concerns across services, designing workflow coordination, splitting reads from writes, or deciding broker topology in event-drive…

name: fsa-ch21-architectural-decisions
description: Applies Chapter 21 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.) on making, justifying, recording and communicating architectural decisions. Covers the Covering Your Assets, Groundhog Day and Email-Driven Architecture antipatterns, the last responsible moment, architectural significance, and Architectural Decision Records (sections, status and RFC, approval criteria, compliance, storage, standards, legacy systems, AI use). Use when deciding whether or when to decide, writing or reviewing an ADR, setting approval rules, or asking an LLM for architecture advice.

name: fsa-ch22-analyzing-risk
description: Applies Chapter 22 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.) on analyzing architecture risk. Covers the impact x likelihood risk matrix, risk assessments by characteristic and domain with totals, filtering and trend direction, three-phase risk storming (identification, consensus, mitigation), unknown-technology scoring, cost-versus-risk negotiation, user-story risk and mitigation patterns. Use when scoring a risk, building a risk report, facilitating or aggregating a risk-storming session, or proposing mitigations.

name: fsa-ch23-diagramming
description: Applies Chapter 23 of Richards and Ford's "Fundamentals of Software Architecture" (2nd ed.) on diagramming architecture. Covers representational consistency across views, the Irrational Artifact Attachment antipattern, low- versus high-fidelity artifacts, tool features and semantic layers, UML, C4 and ArchiMate, and guidelines for titles, lines, shapes, labels, color and keys. Use when drawing, generating (Mermaid, PlantUML, Structurizr) or reviewing an architecture diagram, choosing a notation standard, or planning how to present an architecture to stakeholders.

name: fsa-ch24-making-teams-effective

Use when calibrating architect involvement, diagnosing team dysfunction, drafting team checklists, or setting who decides on libraries and frameworks.

name: fsa-ch25-negotiation-and-leadership

description: Start, check, and fix the local FxA stack on the sandbox VM. Use before a functional test, a screenshot, or any check that needs auth, content, or settings running, and when a service is down or erroring.

name: fxa-storybook-capture
description: Use inside the FxA sandbox VM to screenshot the component states a ticket changed, using Storybook, and hand the files to the host for PR attachment. Trigger when the diff touches a component that has a sibling *.stories.tsx. Not for user flows across pages, which need the full stack.

name: fxa-test-draft
description: Drafts Jest tests for changed code. Defaults to staged/unstaged changes or the most recent commit. Output is a starting point for review, not final.

name: fxa-test-independence
description: Validates that Jest tests in a given file pass both as a full suite and individually in isolation, catching hidden order dependencies and shared mutable state.

name: fxa-test-plan
description: Use inside the FxA sandbox before you change code. Plan how you will prove each behavior the ticket changes, the way a user or client would see it (a functional flow, a direct check against the running stack, an integration spec), with unit tests for edge cases. Write it to /workspace/.fxa-test-plan.json and let /fxa-verify --plan run it. Use again when the plan changes.

name: fxa-test-repair
description: Reviews a test file for violations of FXA testing guidelines, then suggests concrete repairs. Does not auto-apply changes — output is a repair plan for engineer review.

name: fxa-triage
description: Generates a daily FxA triage summary. Queries Jira, GitHub, Bugzilla, and optionally Sentry, then outputs a Slack-ready update with detailed analysis. Use when starting triage duties or preparing the daily triage post. Also offers a dependency alert & bump PR review run that invokes the fxa-dep-triage skill.
allowed_tools: Bash, WebFetch, Skill, mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, mcp__sentry__search_issues, mcp__sentry__search_events, mcp__sentry__find_releases, mcp__sentry__get_sentry_resource, mcp__slack__slack_search_channels, mcp__slack__slack_read_channel, mcp__slack__slack_read_thread, mcp__slack__slack_s

name: fxa-unslop
description: Use inside the FxA sandbox on your own change before the handoff. Checks the diff, the tests and the PR body for what reviewers of FxA agent PRs flag again and again, and fixes it. Run after /code-simplifier and /ponytail-review, and again on the PR body after /humanizer.

name: fxa-verify
description: Verify a change in the FxA monorepo on the sandbox VM with the fastest correct checks. Maps each changed file to its package and runs only the related unit tests, lint, Prettier (it formats them) and a type-check on the changed files, then prints a verdict table. Use before saying tests pass, and before the handoff.

name: fxa-vm-handoff
description: Use inside the FxA sandbox VM to write /workspace/.fxa-auto-done.json, the handoff file the host reads to open the pull request. Run it last, after the PR body is drafted.

name: fxa-vm-selfcheck
description: Use inside the FxA sandbox VM after /fxa-review-quick and before the handoff. Runs the seven checks that FxA reviewers raise most often and that the repo review skills do not cover.

name: fxai-ad-video
description: 广告视频（广告片）制作管线（用户级）。当用户说「做一条广告 / 广告片 / 广告视频 / 宣传片 / 产品视频 / 招商片 / 种草片 / 产品演示 / 10 秒广告 / 品牌片 / 旅游大片」时使用。覆盖：立项（片型·时长·卖点）→ 创意方向与机制 → 口播稿与分镜 → 素材（场景图 / 参考图 / 既有素材）→ 配音与节拍 → 后期包装（标题卡 / 信息贴片 / 片尾品牌卡 / 字幕 / 封面）→ 组装交付。四条路线：产品演示片、品牌蒙太奇、静图运镜旅拍、氛围片。不做：短剧走 fxai-short-drama、MV 走 fxai-mv-pipeline、纯生图走 fxai-comfyui-image-gen、纯数字人口播走 fxai-digital-human-video。

name: fxai-asset-library
description: 应用级素材库管家。管「能直接剪进片子的通用片段」——录屏、演示、对比、口播、实拍、配乐、版式卡、图。库里唯一母版按形态分目录存放，台账记详细规格与用途；检索走 SQLite 倒排索引（中文二元切分 + 字段加权 + 两层召回，万条级毫秒命中），另有缩略图、可预览看板、失联体检；库地址可配置（多库切换）。当用户说「素材库在哪 / 库里有什么 / 找一段开实例的录屏 / 把这段入库 / 换个素材库位置 / 素材台账维护一下 / 快速找素材 / 素材多了检索慢」时使用。只动素材库自身，不动技能包 assets（那是系统级零件）。

name: fxai-asset-registry
description: 可复用素材登记台账。给任何项目目录建一份「素材登记」（人读 md + 机读 json），把界面截图、录屏、成片、对比样片、场景图、角色四视图这类**以后还能再用**的素材登记出来，自动把分段切片、中间渲染、分段配音归成「过程产物」不挡视线。当用户说「这个素材存哪了 / 做个素材登记 / 素材台账 / 有哪些能复用的素材 / 别再到处找了 / 把素材归一下」时使用。只做登记与索引，不移动、不删除、不转码素材。

name: fxai-audio-video
description: 音频驱动视频生成（公共件，MV 与数字人口播共用）。拿一段音频 + 参考图 + 提示词，按 MiniMax H3 三模式（single 单场景 / multi 多场景 / multiref 多参考）出视频。音频是唱歌还是说话与流程无关，只有提示词措辞不同（kind=sing 演唱 / kind=speak 口播）。当需要「用音频生成视频 / 音频驱动的视频 / 复用 MV 那套视频生成 / 逐段音频逐段出视频 / 多段视频拼接」时使用。依赖 fxai-workflow/comfy_client.py 与 fxai-workflow/mv-minimax-*.json。

name: fxai-auto-update
description: 凤希AI 技能包自动更新：请求官网 upgrade/skill.json 拿到版本号与压缩包相对路径，下载整包 zip，解压后逐文件落盘；本地改过的文件不覆盖，交给智能体做三方合并（基线/本地/上游）再落盘；包内专家不落技能根，未安装或版本落后时装进宿主专家市场；支持回滚。当用户说「更新技能包 / 升级技能 / 技能包更新一下 / 检查新版本 / 有没有新版本 / 拉最新版 / 自动更新 / 合并更新 / 回滚技能 / 专家没装 / 把专家也装上 / 检查专家」，或技能包要跟随官网升级时使用。不需要口令或激活码，说人话即触发。不生成技能内容、不动用户项目产物。

name: fxai-browser-publish
description: 自动发布。把项目目录里的最终成片配上封面、标题、简介、标签与 AI 标识，经发布单人工确认后发到各内容平台，并把发布回执写回项目目录。当用户说「发布作品 / 自动发布 / 发到平台 / 召唤发布 / 查发布情况 / 多账号发布 / 发布单 / 接入新平台」时使用；只做发布与回执，不做剪辑、不做生成、不做素材采集。

name: fxai-character-styling
description: 角色造型能力（用户级）。当用户要「选人物+服装+姿势生成角色造型图」「生成穿搭展示图/角色造型照」时使用。把 ai-pose-gallery-zh 项目的提示词写法、风格预设、素材检索整套吸收为自有程序：选人（走角色库 fxai-role-management）、选服装/姿势（本技能登记表检索）、构建提示词、调用场景工作流出图。不做：人物头像生成（走角色库）、视频、发布。

name: fxai-combat-design
description: 战斗设计与动作分镜（用户级）。当用户要「设计打斗剧情 / 动作设计 / 招式设计 / 战斗技能设计 / 战斗分镜 / 空间调度 / 一打多清场 / 双人对招 / 动作术语取词」时使用。流程：提炼创作卡 → 场景抽取 → 动作方案（等用户确认）→ 招式检索（过合理性门禁）→ 招式术语取词 → 技能检索（过条件门禁）→ 剧情仿写 → 编译成稿。产出战斗剧情、动作设计、空间路线与分镜表。不做：任何模型或平台的提示词生成、资料吸收与入库。

name: fxai-comfyui-image-gen
description: 本地 ComfyUI 文生图能力（千问2.1 模板，原生中文提示词）。当用户要求在对话里生成图片、配图、画一张图、出张图、做封面图、用中文提示词生图、给文章/视频/设计配视觉素材时使用。生成的是用户自有角色形象的图（参考图 000 女 / 001 男，规避他人肖像侵权），产物经 HTTP 下载到本地并返回 PNG 路径。仅依赖 ComfyUI HTTP 服务（由 comfy_url 指定，本地或远端均可），提交/探测/下载全部经 HTTP 接口完成，绝不读取 ComfyUI 本机目录；无常驻进程。

name: fxai-comfyui-watcher
description: ComfyUI 任务进度广播监听与「等任务完成」通知（全局共享，零依赖）。当需要「等渲染跑完再继续」「看任务跑到第几镜/百分之几」「一次看到服务器上所有在跑的任务」「拿到产物文件名」时使用；提交任何 ComfyUI 任务（短剧成片、生图、MV、四视图、超分）后都应改用它等待，取代反复 sleep 轮询 /history。主通道是 fxai-toolkit 自己广播的 fxai:progress / fxai:task_saved 事件，按 prompt_id 路由，任何项目共用同一份台账。

name: fxai-common
description: fxai 全系列技能共用的底层公共件（**公共目录，不是技能，没有可触发的能力**）。提供地址规范化、本机代理绕过、统一 HTTP 请求出口、口播文案校验、分段视频的影调/接缝对齐（`video_tone.py`）、最终交付编码（`video_encode.py`）与 AIGC 隐式标识写入/验收（`aigc_mark.py`）。当需要知道「fxai-common 是什么、哪些技能依赖它、它提供哪些函数」时使用。普通用户无需安装说明它的用法——它由 fxai-workflow / fxai-voiceover / fxai-comfyui-watcher / fxai-audio-video / fxai-digital-human-video / fxai-voiceover-script 自动 import。

name: fxai-content-review
description: 内容复盘与经验库。对一条已发布（或已写好）的内容做诊断，把结论按岗位领域结构化写进 SQLite 台账，同类问题在本领域内自动累加「第几次出现」，按领域导出经验库_领域.md 供对应岗位技能开工前读取，并支持把反复命中的经验晋升为规则。当用户说「复盘这条视频 / 这篇文章」「看下这条为什么没爆」「记一条经验」「经验库里有什么」「顽疾有哪些」「这条该不该写成规矩」「登记素材 / 补素材缺口」时使用。也用于素材打标签与素材库台账维护。；不做：只登记本地最终产物，不生成内容。

name: fxai-digital-human-video
description: 数字人口播视频生成（口播音频 → 数字人出镜讲话的视频）。当用户要求「口播视频 / 数字人视频 / 数字人出镜 / 单场景·多场景·多段口播」时使用。音频来自 fxai-voiceover 或用户提供；单音频出一条，多音频逐段各一条再拼接。生成复用 fxai-audio-video（与 MV 同一套 H3 实现）。不做：MV（→fxai-mv-pipeline）、纯配音（→fxai-voiceover）、短剧（→fxai-short-drama）。

name: fxai-face-edit
description: 人脸替换 / 修复 / 增强 / 整片角色替换：换脸、唇形同步、老照片修复上色、人脸增强、背景移除、整片视频人脸精修（本机 ComfyUI 分段链）、整片视频换人换装（MiniMax H3 分段角色替换，保留原动作与运镜）、全场景替换（人、场景、道具、配乐整套换掉）。当用户要求「把 A 的脸换成 B」「给这段视频换脸」「让这个人说这段话」「人脸更清晰一点」「整条片子精修一遍」「把这个视频里的人换成参考图那个人」「角色替换」「换掉主角」「全场景替换 / 换全部场景 / 场景道具都换掉」「主体替换 / 仅替换主体 / 只换主体」「删掉画面里某个人」「去掉另一个人」「只留一位」「删除指定人物」时使用。三条链路：FaceFusion REST（云端，换脸 / 对嘴 / 单图）、本机分段精修（只修脸）、本机分段角色替换（H3 换人 LoRA，身份与服装一起换）。只按地址发 HTTP，不启停服务。不做：生图配图（→fxai-comfyui-image-gen）、数字人口播（→fxai-digital-human-video）、建实例与开关机（→fxai-xiangongyun-deploy）。

name: fxai-fourview-gen
description: 生成角色四视图/三视图。四视图必须提供角色参考图；三视图参考图可选（有参考→按参考人物生成，无参考→按提示词纯设定生成）；三视图与四视图使用各自【独立工作流】（img-qwen21-threeview.json / img-qwen21-fourview.json，互不复用）。当其它技能或脚本需要"一致人物形象的角色视图参考图"时调用——例如 MV 多参考模式的人物绑定、短剧/数字人口播的角色三视图建档、动画角色设定。跨项目通用，依赖共享客户端 fxai-workflow/comfy_client.py。；不做：不生成视频，只产出角色参考视图。

name: fxai-h3-video-prompt
description: MiniMax Hailuo H3 视频提示词写作规范（用户级，通用）。覆盖我们用到的两条分支——【首尾帧 FL2VA + 音频参考】（单场景/多场景）与【全参考 Ref2VA + 音频参考】（多参考），并强调"音频=原音频、不另行设计音轨"、"提示词必须契合文案内容与场景（含道具）"；另有「中文对白镜头（短剧分镜）写法硬规范」，覆盖站位/距离/视线/谁对谁说话/台词归属/运镜顺序。需要为自建 MiniMax 数字人 MV / 数字人口播视频写或审 H3 提示词、写/审短剧分镜提示词、排查人物/场景不一致或镜头乱动时使用。MV 与数字人口播共用这一套规范；配合 fxai-audio-video / fxai-mv-pipeline / fxai-digital-human-video / fxai-short-drama 使用；**打斗镜另需先向 fxai-combat-design 取招式术语与物理短语**（取词契约见 `references/05` / `06` 册与铁律 11）；**触发词（Combat V2 / Camera Motion LoRA）挂载见 `references/07` 册与铁律 13**——短剧管线 `build_lines_data(auto_triggers=True)` 已按镜型自动挂载，MV / 口播走 `build_ref2va_prompt…

name: fxai-image-to-jpeg
description: 把 PNG/源图转成最高质量 JPEG（quality=95 + subsample=0/4:4:4 + optimize=True），用于公众号/文章配图、上传前压体积。跨项目公共技能，纯 PIL 实现，不依赖任何项目本地路径。当用户说"转 JPEG / 压成高清图 / 图片转 JPG 上传 / 公众号配图转格式"时使用。；不做：不做设计与排版，只转格式。

name: fxai-infocard
description: 给任意视频叠加「信息贴片」——半透明形状（卡片/气泡/胶囊/便签/绶带/尖标签/书签/纸签/下划线/括号）的辅助性补充内容层，按时间码出现在画面任意位置，带淡入/滑入/弹入 + 停留 + 淡出。当用户要求「加信息贴片 / 贴个说明 / 加补充提示 / 名词解释卡 / 加提示卡片 / 补充信息卡 / 加对话气泡 / 加关键词胶囊 / 把补充说明贴上去」时使用。与产线无关，任何视频都能叠。不负责字幕（fxai-lyric-subtitle）、不负责标题卡（fxai-title-card）、不负责封面。

name: fxai-lyric-subtitle
description: (视频字幕) 给 MV / 视频加标准歌词字幕。当用户说"给视频加字幕 / 歌词字幕 / 字幕烧录 / 卡拉OK 字幕 / 给 MV 加歌词"时使用。覆盖：whisper 提取时间戳 → 歌词文字校正 → 生成 SRT/ASS → 用带 libass 的 ffmpeg 烧录。全程本地处理，不上传视频。

name: fxai-material-collect
description: 素材采集。给一条网页链接，把页面上的视频与图集取回本地，供分镜拆解、角色替换、剪辑使用。当用户说「扒下来 / 抓取视频 / 下载这个链接 / 采集素材 / 把这条存到本地 / 按链接取素材」时使用；只负责取素材，不负责剪辑、转码、换脸与发布。

name: fxai-mixed-layout
description: fxai 混排视频的公共件（**公共目录，不是技能，没有可触发的能力**）。装的是「版式槽 + 素材槽」：槽里可以填图片（单图 / 多图轮播）、视频片段、或一整页网页（文字卡 / 长图滚动 / 真网页 / 自定义 HTML），最后都归一成一条同尺寸的无声视频流，交给外层去叠壳、叠字幕、拼接。被 fxai-slide-video（上中下分栏等版式）、fxai-ad-video（广告片的混排段）、fxai-poster（网页模式）自动 import。当需要「加一种新的展示形式」「改素材槽行为」「查版式登记表」时读这里；普通用户不需要直接调用它。

name: fxai-mv-pipeline
description: 音乐→图片→MV 一体化生成管线（用户级公共能力）。当用户说「做首歌出个 MV / 生成音乐并配视频 / 用 MiniMax 生成数字人 MV / 单场景·多场景·多参考 MV / 给我做个音乐短视频」时使用。覆盖：音乐生成（Yue2 默认 / MiniMax Music 3 支持男女对唱）→ 千问2.1 生成人物与场景图 → MiniMax 三种模式（单场景/多场景/多参考）MV 视频生成，所有提示词中文。不做：口播视频（走 fxai-digital-human-video）、短剧（走 fxai-short-drama）、纯生图（走 fxai-comfyui-image-gen）、只生歌不出片（走 fxai-yue2）。

name: fxai-novel-writing
description: 小说创作（短篇 / 长篇）与封面图。当用户要「写小说 / 短篇小说 / 长篇小说 / 连载 / 小说大纲 / 创作思路 / 章节梗概 / 目录 / 人物画像 / 人物设定 / 小说封面 / 封面图 / 封面提示词 / 发番茄小说 / 投稿各大小说平台」时使用。产出：短篇正文（单文件，≥8000 汉字）、长篇档案（目录 + 创作思路 + 人物画像 + 逐章梗概 + 分章正文）、封面图与封面提示词。不做：短剧剧本与分镜 → fxai-short-drama-script；封面出图 → 调 fxai-comfyui-image-gen。

name: fxai-onethingai-deploy

description: 세그먼트 1개를 받아 대표 1곳의 제안 메일 문안을 만들고 그룹 전체로 확장한 뒤, 일본어 발신 문안의 번역을 별도 단위로 검증하고, 승인 화면을 만들어 **사람 승인 지점에서 종료**한다. 승인이 기록된 뒤 발송 모드로 다시 부르면 승인 여부를 별도 단위(Read 전용)로 판독한 뒤 그 건만 발송 기록을 남긴다. 제안 메일 제작·발송(G5) 설계서를 그대로 실행하는 호출 계약이다. 사용자가 "제안 메일 만들어줘", "G5 돌려줘", "승인했어 이어서 보내줘"라고 할 때도 이 스킬이다.

name: g5-제안메일제작발송
description: 세그먼트 1개를 받아 대표 1곳의 제안 메일 문안을 만들고 그룹 전체로 확장한 뒤, 일본어 발신 문안의 번역을 별도 단위로 검증하고, 승인 화면을 만들어 **사람 승인 지점에서 종료**한다. 승인이 기록된 뒤 발송 모드로 다시 부르면 승인 여부를 별도 단위(Read 전용)로 판독한 뒤 그 건만 발송 기록을 남긴다. 제안 메일 제작·발송(G5) 설계서를 그대로 실행하는 호출 계약이다. 사용자가 "제안 메일 만들어줘", "G5 돌려줘", "승인했어 이어서 보내줘"라고 할 때도 이 스킬이다.

name: g5k
description: Operating Grid'5000 (g5k) for experiment campaigns. Covers OAR reservations, the day/night usage policy, autonomous daytime iteration jobs for AI agents, non-interactive run patterns over SSH, GNU-parallel distributed runs, monitoring, syncing results back, and home-directory cleanup. Use whenever work involves Grid5000 (any site alias like nancy.g5k or lyon.g5k), reserving nodes, launching or monitoring runs, extending or releasing reservations, syncing outputs, or planning an experiment campaign.

name: g5k-launch
description: Decide where on Grid5000 to run a test, training or eval job, and launch it there — reuse a running node, else find free GPUs on every Grid5000 site (Abaca: Grenoble/Nancy/Rennes/Sophia; SLICES-FR default queue: Lille/Lyon/Nantes) with scripts/g5k_gpus.py and submit where the job starts soonest. Use whenever you need to run pytest or any GPU/heavy command, launch or relaunch a training/eval job, when the thoth GPUs (Grenoble vercors) are full or a job waits in the queue, or when asked where GPUs are free.

name: g6
description: VS-Enhanced Academic Style Humanizer - Transforms writing patterns to achieve authentic scholarly voice Applies transformations from G5 analysis to create natural academic prose Use when: improving AI-assisted writing quality, preparing manuscripts, enhancing scholarly voice Triggers: humanize, transform, make natural, improve writing quality, improve style

name: g6-abstraction
description: Use when each evaluation in a black-box search is costly (a training run, a simulation, a benchmark), you hold a trace of configurations already evaluated with their scores, and you are about to spend more budget on blind trial and error; it fits a checked model of the score landscape to the trace, measures on the recorded trace what pruning would have saved or lost, and gives guarded advice on which fresh candidates cannot beat the incumbent.

name: g6-action-gating
description: Use when an agent proposes an outward action and needs a deterministic decision before acting, when a workflow must stay inside the bounds a person reviewed it for, or when the person wants per-run operation count limits and injected safeguards that can only tighten that decision.

name: g6-action-logic
description: Use when an agent or workflow is about to take a large or hard-to-undo step and must check that it has a complete plan to observe, stop and roll it back, that it does not collide with other actions in flight, that no warning signal is being ignored, or that it is not still relying on a hypothesis an outcome has already disproved.

name: g6-adapt-audio
description: Use when you need to cut, join, mix, fade, level, equalise, compress, limit, gate, de-ess, de-noise, resample or convert a WAV, or measure its loudness, true peak, pitch, tempo, spectrum or silences, and you want every result measured again before you use it, never clipped silently.

name: g6-adapt-automl
description: Use when you want the best of several scikit-learn estimators and their settings for a table, found by a bounded, seeded search (a time budget and a trial cap) that compares settings by cross-validation on training rows only, with the winner measured on rows the tool held out itself against a baseline, and a missing search engine refused rather than silently replaced.

name: g6-adapt-bayesian
description: Use when a scalar beta-binomial, gamma-Poisson or normal mean model needs an explicit posterior, credible interval, prior sensitivity, predictive check or checked sampling, and a point estimate would hide uncertainty.

name: g6-adapt-blender
description: Use when you need a 3D scene built, lit, rendered or exported (OBJ, STL, GLB, FBX) with the Blender the person installed, and you want every change read back from Blender's scene and every render and export inspected before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-comfyui
description: Use when you need a picture made or edited from a text prompt by a diffusion model on the ComfyUI server the person runs on this machine (text to image, image to image, inpainting, upscaling, or your own ComfyUI workflow), with every picture fetched into G6's media folder and checked before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-diagrams
description: Use when you need a diagram (a flowchart, a sequence of messages, a graph, a component map, a box, tree or table in plain text) written as Mermaid, Graphviz DOT, PlantUML or ASCII that will not break on a quote or a keyword, or drawn by Graphviz into an SVG or PNG you can trust holds every node you declared.

name: g6-adapt-django
description: Use when drafting consistent Django model, view, URL, admin, form, serializer and settings source, then checking a complete project in the sandbox.

name: g6-adapt-ffmpeg
description: Use when you need to convert, cut, join, resize, retime, filter, subtitle or level a video or sound file with ffmpeg, or pull out its sound or a frame, and you want every file ffmpeg writes measured against what you asked for before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-generative-art
description: Use when you need an actual picture file and not a description of one (procedural art, a texture, a pattern, a fractal, a vector drawing or a terrain mesh for a 3D scene), made on this machine with no model, no network and no cost, from a seed you can reproduce, and checked before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-healing
description: Use when one step of Python code fails with an error you have tests for, and an agent wants a model to repair it without a careless automatic fix; the error is triaged first, the patch is checked in the sandbox on tests the model sees, and it is kept only if it passes held-back tests the model never saw.

name: g6-adapt-image
description: Use when you need to resize, crop, rotate, flip, recolour, combine or convert a picture, measure one strictly, or have one generated (locally through ComfyUI or a procedural technique, or by a paid image service only when G6's action gate allows the payment), and you want every resulting file checked before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-library-synthesizer
description: Use when translating a paper's algorithm into a Python module and checking it against examples supplied independently by the caller.

name: g6-adapt-pandas
description: Use when you are handed a table (CSV text, JSON rows or a list of rows) and need to know, before you compute anything from it, which columns are numbers, text or a mix, which values only look missing, which codes have leading zeros, and which rows or keys repeat, read by one stated rule with nothing converted or dropped silently.

name: g6-adapt-physical-ai
description: Use when a robot motion plan or grasp, from a model, a planner or a person, is about to be carried out and you need to know whether it collides along its segments, leaves its workspace, breaks a joint or speed limit, misses its goal, or lets an object slip or crush, against the robot's own specification and a stated world.

name: g6-adapt-pytorch
description: Use when you need a small neural network trained on rows of data without writing the training loop yourself, and need its score measured on rows held out by the tool itself, against a baseline, with the run seeded and stopped the moment its loss breaks, so a training accuracy, a diverged loss or a leaky feature never passes for a result.

name: g6-adapt-rq
description: Use when you need to submit an operator-registered background job, inspect queue reports or recover selected failed jobs, with JSON arguments, operator permission and a separately managed Redis or Valkey server and POSIX worker.

name: g6-adapt-sklearn
description: Use when you need to fit a scikit-learn model to rows of data, or compare a few, and need its score measured on rows held out by the tool itself, against a baseline, with an interval, after checks for target leakage, repeated rows, class imbalance and a fixed seed, so a training score or a leaky feature never passes for a result.

name: g6-adapt-synth
description: Use when you need a tone, a note, a chord, an arpeggio, a scale, a short melody, noise or a drum pattern as a WAV file, or want a few words read into musical parameters, and you want each sound measured against what you asked for before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-visualisation
description: Use when you need a chart of rows of data (a line, bars, a scatter, a histogram, box plots or a heat map) as an SVG, PNG or self-contained HTML file, and need to know it shows every row you gave and only the values you gave, with nothing dropped silently and no script in the file.

name: g6-adapt-voice
description: Use when you need text spoken into a WAV file (a local voice first, a paid one only when the person's key file and G6's action gate allow it), or a recording transcribed by a paid service, and you want each voice inspected, and a transcript refused when it is empty or too fast for the speech in the clip (its words are not checked), before you use it.

name: g6-adapt-webpage
description: Use when building an offline web page or design-token set and checking markup, declared colour contrast and optional horizontal overflow.

name: g6-agent-autogen
description: Use when a task should be worked by a team of AutoGen agents (taking turns, picked by a model, or handing the task over) on a model the person passes in, with a message limit G6's trusted policy caps, every tool call decided by G6's gate, G6's stop checked after every message, and the team's answer kept as a draft to check.

name: g6-agent-claude
description: Use when a coding task should be handed to Anthropic's Claude Code, the command-line coding agent the person installed and signed in to, in one project folder, with its own tools named on every run (read tools only unless edits are granted, never its shell or web tools), a deadline, G6's stop, and its own report kept as a claim to check.

name: g6-agent-codex
description: Use when a coding task should be handed to OpenAI's Codex, the command-line coding agent the person installed and signed in to, in one project folder, with no more access than the task needs (read-only unless writes are granted), a deadline, G6's stop, and Codex's own report kept as a claim to check.

name: g6-agent-langgraph
description: Use when a multi-step workflow should run as a LangGraph graph that saves its state after every step under G6's state folder, so a run that is stopped, killed or fails resumes where it was without repeating finished steps, with every tool call decided by G6's gate, llm steps only on a model the person passes in, and the result kept as a draft to check.

name: g6-agent-nanoclaw
description: Use when several agents must pass messages to one another durably (groups of named members, messages to one member or to all, optionally typed), with every message reaching its reader at least once, in order, a page at a time, coming back until it is acknowledged, a retried send stored once, and none reaching the wrong member.

name: g6-agent-runtime
description: Use when an agent runtime (a coding agent's command line, a framework's agent loop, your own adapter) is to run a task under limits a person set, with every tool call decided before it runs, the run stoppable, every failure handled the same way, and the agent's own "done" kept as a claim rather than taken as proof.

name: g6-agent-smolagents
description: Use when a task suits a smolagents agent, either calling declared tools or writing Python to work it out, on a model the person passes in, with every tool call decided by G6's gate and every code step held to a restricted syntax and run in a bounded child process (a clean environment, a time limit, no network, a fixed import list), never in G6's process, and the answer kept as a draft to check.

name: g6-algebra
description: Use when an answer, a test expectation or code rests on a symbolic calculation (simplifying, factoring, solving an equation, a derivative, an integral, a limit, a series, a matrix's determinant, inverse or eigenvalues, or an integer's factors, primality or greatest common divisor) and you are about to state the result from your own working.

name: g6-algorithm-design
description: Use when a task needs an algorithm and you want catalogued textbook options that fit the stated problem, each with the preconditions it needs, the cost it claims and the proof obligations it leaves, bound to the requirements a change must keep, instead of a method invented on the spot or one called optimal without proof.

name: g6-align-prompt-library
description: Use when prompts, specifications or evaluation sets must be kept with their full history, each version addressed by the SHA-256 of its content so a result can cite exactly the version it used, with strict template rendering, tombstones instead of deletes and rollback as a new version.

name: g6-australian-legal-corpus
description: Use when an agent must find what Australian legislation or a court decision says, in the text itself with its citation, jurisdiction, link and collection date, rather than from memory; it searches a local copy of the Open Australian Legal Corpus, refuses Victoria, the ACT, the Northern Territory and any jurisdiction it lacks instead of answering with another's law, and says every time that the text is a dated snapshot, not current law and not legal advice.

name: g6-causal
description: Use when an answer says one thing causes, drives or improves another, or estimates an effect from data, and you are about to choose which variables to control for, call an effect identifiable, or report a causal number from a correlation, a regression or your own reading of a diagram.

name: g6-cegis
description: Use when code has a fixed shape with a few unknown parts (constants, a sign, a comparison, a choice between strings) and you are about to pick those parts by hand from a handful of examples, or to trust generated code because it passed the examples it was written from.

name: g6-coding-agent-gate
description: Use when a coding agent is about to act on a risky plan (a deploy, auth or security, credentials, a data migration, payment, medical or legal logic, skipping or disabling a check) or is about to report coding work as done, and the plan or the drafted answer must be checked against the evidence the agent actually has.

name: g6-cog-arch-actr
description: Use when an agent keeps many memories and needs them ranked the way human memory ranks them, by how recently and how often each was used and by the current context, with a recall refused when nothing is strong enough, or when a small rule set must consult that memory step by step and be judged by a goal test.

name: g6-cog-arch-aixi
description: Use when trying a model-based planning agent design on a small environment and it must be judged by a test rather than by argument, so an agent acting on a model that has not learned the environment's rewards is caught by its regret against a random policy on the same seed.

name: g6-cog-arch-gps
description: Use when an agent needs a short sequence of steps to reach a goal from declared actions (each with preconditions, what it adds and what it removes), or must check a plan someone else wrote, a model's included, step by step before acting on it, so a plan that skips a precondition or undoes an earlier goal is caught before anyone follows it.

name: g6-cognitive-bridge
description: Use when an agent must choose which way to check a research or engineering claim (a rule graph, a causal model, a formal check, a predictive model or an optimisation), rank discriminating probes between competing hypotheses, or assemble the evidence for a claim against a pinned standard, with the choice and the evidence kept apart from the agent that made the claim.

name: g6-complexity
description: Use when a coding agent is about to change a Python package and you need to know, before it runs anything, which modules, shared state and side effects the change can reach, which of your stated requirements it must keep, and which pieces of state you marked avoidable could be simplified.

name: g6-component-creator
description: Use when an agent is starting a new G6 component, wrapping a Python library as one, or about to call a component package done, and needs the library's own shape scaffolded (declarations, a typed input, refusing handlers, a failing test, a skill whose ops match) or a package checked against the library's standard first.

name: g6-context
description: Use when repository files, retrieved passages, notes, subagent output or a long conversation are about to go into a model call and could overflow the budget, bury the task, carry secrets, or carry instructions the model should only read; or when an error report from a traceback must not leak code or personal data.

name: g6-csf
description: Use when an agent's plan could reach a harmful state and nobody has worked out how likely that is: write the agent as a small model of states and transition probabilities with the unsafe states named, then get an upper bound on reaching one within N steps, check a temporal property on a trace or on every path, check whether the plan's operations can be undone, or checkpoint a git working tree before risky edits.

name: g6-ctx-ace
description: Use when an agent must keep notes or lessons across steps or sessions and find the relevant ones again later, so an old but relevant note is not buried under newer ones, a stale note is not used as current, a note planted from injected text comes back flagged with its writer and source marked as claims, and a lesson nobody approved is held back.

name: g6-ctx-cognee
description: Use when facts an agent needs are spread across several texts with nothing linking them, and the person runs a Cognee server, to add the texts to it, search it, and follow the chain of links Cognee's graph draws from a fact in one text to a related fact in another, each result untrusted and cited as far as Cognee allows.

name: g6-ctx-colbert
description: Use when an agent must rank a set of passages it holds by meaning rather than shared words (a question worded differently from the text that answers it), and must know which method ranked them, so word matching never stands in silently for meaning, model weights are never downloaded behind its back, and nothing from one call's passages is kept for the next.

name: g6-ctx-contexthub
description: Use when an agent should answer from a versioned documentation registry the person trusts (context-hub's registry.json format), with each document's date, version and time to live kept, so a copy past its time to live is refused rather than used as current, and notes stay apart from the documents.

name: g6-ctx-elastic
description: Use when an agent must search, read or count documents in an Elasticsearch server the person runs, over fields the index's mapping really holds, so a query that cannot match is refused instead of answered with no hits, a partial answer says so, and every hit comes back as untrusted text with its address on the server.

name: g6-ctx-geo
description: Use when an agent must answer a location question (an address, a point, a route, a distance, a height, a time zone) from a map service rather than from memory, and must know when the service refused the key or ran out of quota rather than found nothing; paid calls go out only on the action gate's allow and the person's key file.

name: g6-ctx-git
description: Use when an agent must read or change a git repository and every call must leave a record, or must find out what changed in a working copy since a point, whoever changed it, so changes an agent made behind the record are not missed; git runs with the repository's own programs switched off, only in folders the person declared.

name: g6-ctx-langextract
description: Use when an agent must pull named fields (a date, a reference, an amount, a name) out of free text and needs each value tied to where it sits in the text, so a value the model invented or reworded is refused or flagged rather than passed as found, and a long text is read whole, never cut off (a field the model leaves empty is reported not checked: a fact it passes over is not caught).

name: g6-ctx-library-mapper
description: Use when an agent is about to write code for a method that may already exist as a library, or is choosing a dependency, and must find candidate libraries in PyPI, GitHub and Hugging Face with the licence each declares, and look those licences up against the project's own; a source that could not be asked is never read as "no library exists".

name: g6-ctx-search
description: Use when an agent must search the web and know exactly what came back, so an engine that failed, was blocked or ran out of quota is never read as "there are no results", no other engine silently answers in its place, and a paid search engine is used only with the person's own key.

name: g6-ctx-vision
description: Use when an agent must see what is in a picture (describe it, answer a question about it, read its text, list its objects) through an image-capable model it was given, and must keep the model's account as a claim, with the picture checked before it is sent and the text reading cross-checked by Tesseract when that matters.

name: g6-database
description: Use when you need to read or change data in a database the person running G6 has declared (SQLite by default, DuckDB for large datasets or files, PostgreSQL), and want reads that cannot write, changes dry-run first in one transaction, destructive statements refused unless the server allows them, and bounded results that say when they were cut.

name: g6-datalog
description: Use when an answer depends on what follows from a set of facts and rules (permissions, eligibility, dependencies, reachability, policy, family or ownership relations) and you are about to say that something does or does not follow, or to list everything that does, from your own reading of the rules.

name: g6-debate
description: Use when an agent is about to accept one model's first answer to a judgement question (a plan, a design trade-off, a go or no-go) and wants role-named critics to push on it in turn, with dissent surfaced and an honest reading of how far the turns agree, which is never a check that an answer is right.

name: g6-decision-making
description: Use when an agent must choose what to try next (which experiment, which arm, which action in a small known model) or how many times to retry each task within a budget, and the choice must be a standard rule with its working shown and the same answer on every run, rather than an ad hoc guess.

name: g6-delivery-status-judging
description: 발송 기록 1건과 그 건에 대한 메일 시스템 응답(바운스 코드·회신 도착 여부)을 받아 [대기중]/[회신]/[무응답]/[주소 오류] 넷 중 하나로 상태를 판정하고, G7 정정 신호가 오면 그 판정을 되돌린다. 발송 결과 판정(G6) 설계서와 판정 기준 카드를 그대로 실행하는 호출 계약이다. 같은 발송 건을 시간을 두고 다시 조회하는 반복 실행이다. 사용자가 "바운스 왔어", "발송 결과 확인해줘", "G6 돌려줘", "자동응답이었대 정정해줘"라고 할 때도 이 스킬이다.

name: g6-design-governance
description: Use when an agent has changed a codebase's structure (moved code, added imports, split a module) and must check before reporting it done that it added no import cycle, broke no layer rule and added no wrapper that only forwards its arguments; it reads a file map you give for any package and refuses rather than calling a check with nothing to check clean.

name: g6-distillation
description: Use when a small generated or distilled Python function (a solve(x) meant to replace a model call or a hand-written rule) is about to be relied on, and you need to know whether it holds on cases it was not made from, run out of process under a time and memory bound.

name: g6-duty-of-care
description: Use when an agent works with people who may be in distress (a support chat, a care or clinical intake, a wellbeing check, a carer's notes) and must not miss signs that a vulnerable person is at risk of suicide, self-harm, harming someone else or a child being in danger; or when a PHQ-9 or GAD-7 needs adding up exactly as its form prints it; or when a dated crisis line for a region is needed.

name: g6-epistemic-integrity
description: Use when a conclusion is about to be stated or acted on and its confidence must match its evidence, such as a recommendation someone will act on, a health, legal, security or financial claim, an irreversible step, a percentage without its baseline, causal language, or several sources that may all repeat one origin.

name: g6-evidence
description: Use when a piece of work (a patch, a report, any artifact) must be given a completion state that says only what its checks support, with every gap named, or when a certificate someone hands you must be checked for consistency with the artifact's bytes.

name: g6-formal
description: Use when an answer rests on a logical step that must be exactly right, such as whether premises entail a conclusion, whether constraints can all hold, a counterexample to a claim, two conditions being equivalent, which requirements conflict, or a small optimum over integer or real constraints, and you are about to argue it in words instead of deciding it.

name: g6-gate-execution
description: G6发布阶段门禁执行器，统一运行构建制品校验和回滚手册完整性检查并汇总结果

name: g6-goal-engine
description: Use when an agent loop runs a long, multi-step goal and must check before each step that it is still inside its declared token, time and disk limits, that the action it is about to take is allowed, and that a person has signed off at the points named in advance; it reads declared controls against what the executor reports and executes nothing itself.

name: g6-graph-reasoning
description: Use when conclusions spread over a graph of people, services, accounts or documents from facts that are only partly certain (trust, risk, popularity, reliability scores) and you are about to state how sure a conclusion is, or to combine rules that might contradict each other, from your own reading.

name: g6-grounding
description: Use when a draft (an AI answer, a report, an email, a summary) states facts, figures or quotes that should come from documents you hold, and each sentence must be matched to a source sentence, with wrong numbers and flipped negations flagged, or must rest on more than one independent source, before it goes out.

name: g6-guards
description: Use when untrusted text (user input, a retrieved page, a tool result, a planner's output, an action's arguments) is about to reach an agent or a policy check and needs a cheap advisory flag for prompt injection, a request for the system prompt or an instruction to switch off a safeguard, or when code is reviewed for lines that quietly defeat a safety chain.

name: g6-harness
description: Use when a task or sequence of steps needs frozen acceptance checks, observed failures, readiness measurements, or a report of which failed criterion to address next.

name: g6-hat-orchestrator
description: Use when coordinating declared team capabilities, task reports and readiness barriers, while keeping authority in an operator-owned roster and escalating ties or possible real-world actions to a person through G6 action gating.

name: g6-intent-engine
description: Use when an agent is about to start on a request whose purpose, standard of success, unacceptable outcomes, scope or risk tolerance it has not been told, and should ask the person instead of reading the request its own way; or when it needs the intent contract a mission or intake is held to.

name: g6-invariants
description: Use when a result envelope (from a G6 component, your own tool or another agent) is about to be trusted, passed on or asserted in a test, and you need to know whether its completion_state, warning_card, evidence, request_id and run_id agree with one another, or whether a set of checks passed only because none of them ran.

name: g6-knowledge-chunker
description: Use when a document is to be split into passages for indexing or citation and every passage must be traceable to the exact words of its source, or when a citation an agent holds (offsets and text) must be checked against the document it names before it is quoted.

name: g6-knowledge-converter
description: Use when a PDF, a web page, Markdown or a text file must be read as text an agent can cite, and it matters what was not read, so a page without a text layer, hidden page text or a format nothing converts is reported rather than silently dropped or read as empty.

name: g6-knowledge-fetcher
description: Use when an agent must read a web page or search arXiv, an OAI-PMH repository, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar, and must know exactly what came back, so a blocked, failed or cut-short fetch is never read as "there is nothing", and fetched text is kept as untrusted data rather than instructions.

name: g6-knowledge-indexer
description: Use when an agent must keep many cited passages searchable between calls within a storage budget it sets, and find them again with each hit's source and a score whose scale is stated, so an index never outgrows its budget and an index that holds nothing or failed is never read as "no match".

description: Criticar jogos em polimento, investigando foco, mecânicas, desafio, progressão, repetição, descoberta e motivos de continuidade ou abandono com pesquisa e evidências. Especialmente útil para aventuras de mineração, ação rítmica e roguelites; não implementa mudanças automaticamente.

name: gameplay-crouch-zone-assistance
description: 为已有蹲伏控制的玩家角色添加关卡碰撞区域辅助：进入低矮通道时贡献模拟蹲伏请求，复用原控制器并安全释放；不用于 NPC 决策、通用输入系统或边缘停挂。

name: gameplay-cut-surface-rendering
description: 当游戏切割产生开放截面、错误外皮材质或圆形木芯不贴合不规则轮廓时，组织新暴露面的封口与材质边界校对；不提供切割触发、通用三角化或物理断裂算法。

name: gameplay-dash-feedback
description: 当冲刺速度存在但路径、起止或角色轮廓难读时，组合方向形变、残像与速度线并做样式对照；不因幽灵外观新增无敌或改变实际移动规则。

name: gameplay-dash-roll-momentum
description: 仅在明确要求真实移动规则时，实现向下冲刺接地转翻滚的速度交接，以及翻滚中冲刺消费储存动量的短时加速；不用于普通冲刺残像或落地重量润色。

name: gameplay-decorative-waterfall
description: 为明确选择装饰性常流水的场景实现半砖湖缘触发、空中瀑布绘制与地面截断，保持源湖和下游液体量不受影响；不用于真实液体转移、水洼贴地网格或机器表面动画。

name: gameplay-deformable-support
description: 当车轮等载荷需要在可弯曲、可压缩的承载面上保持接触时，设计连接刚体层与层间弹簧的局部原型及稳定性验收；不是固定碰撞体的视觉压扁、通用软体算法或物性标定教程。

name: gameplay-design
description: 玩法内容策划技能。生成核心循环、战斗系统、成长系统等玩法设计文档， 并提供对应的 GDScript 代码模板。

name: gameplay-design
description: signal damage_dealt(attacker, target, damage)

name: gameplay-design
description: Create or revise game actions, controls, actor behavior and knowledge, spaces, encounters, shared timing, or free audiovisual play. Use for an executable action contract, behavior, layout, encounter or controllable phrase. Skip pure economy, lore, subscription policy, technical refactors and wording changes that leave these game relationships unchanged.

name: gameplay-design-orchestrator
description: 当游戏创意仍处于完整规格说明的上游阶段，需要顶层的游戏玩法设计流程时使用： 锁定方向、按序执行阶段，并整合为一个游戏玩法设计包。 这是全新游戏设计工作的常规入口。不适用于非游戏产品设计或直接实现。

name: gameplay-design-verification
description: 用可计算的量回答玩法设计的两个硬问题——① 设计期：这个玩法到底有没有决策空间（写任何 UI 之前，用 随机/贪心/规划/全知 四层策略跑分布，测规划增益、技能表达、UX 体检三项指标；含十条可复用判据，以及难度「内容带≠阶梯」、通过线画在哪、数值可达性等设计错误）② 实现期：AI 真的按最优策略行动吗（先证局面结构性质、再写闭式解，用暴力博弈树 DP 逐个状态交叉验证，从交付文件抽取求解器代码块防测试漂移，双方最优自对弈端到端对账，UI 门控状态机单独测）。含两侧统一的断言纪律与变异测试（四种失效模式、等价变异必须存活、假断言三形态）。当用户说"这个玩法没深度""高手新手分数差不多""随便玩和认真玩一样""一局只有两三步""关数太少""太简单""几秒钟就玩完了""加了限时还是没深度""设计新的策略/资源管理/卡牌/规划/推理/解谜类玩法""优化 AI 让它走最优解""AI 不够聪明/像在乱走""这个博弈题的 AI 是错的"时使用。

name: gameplay-designer
description: Design and balance pacman-256's team-based maze gameplay, movement, contact rules, pickups, and game feel. Use when designing levels, mechanics, balancing, or tuning gameplay.

name: gameplay-designer
description: Gameplay Designer (Star-Lord): The fun engineer. Dispatch when the War Room seats this role.

name: gameplay-dialogue-presentation
description: 当逐字对话、标点节奏、情绪强调或重显后的文字进度不清时组织文本显示与动画生命周期；区分显隐、句子进度和真正继续操作，不接管剧情分支与 NPC 交互规则。

name: gameplay-dynamic-carry-alignment
description: 实现可变长短、粗细的世界物体携带：按重量分组选择姿态，校准局部长轴、厚度轴和锚点，按实际截面调整手部贴合并在放下时清理绑定；不用于固定工具挥动或物品入库反馈。

name: gameplay-economy-anti-exploit
description: Review gameplay economies for duplication exploits, transaction ordering flaws, reward farming loops, and unintended resource creation.

name: gameplay-employee-needs
description: Employee needs system for BlastSimulator2026: single fatigue gauge, morale effects, collapse and interruption, proactive queue insertion, building replenishment and shift cycles. Use when implementing or modifying employee well-being, rest mechanics, living quarters replenishment, or shift systems.

name: gameplay-employee-skills
description: Employee skills and task queue system for BlastSimulator2026: skill categories, proficiency levels (1-5), XP gain, task duration formula, pending-action pool, ghost preview rendering, and in-scene task progress bars. Use when implementing or modifying employee qualifications, task dispatch, action queuing, or proficiency mechanics.

name: gameplay-engineer
description: Phaser 3 TypeScript 게임의 룸·전투·소환·조합·분대 UI 기능을 최소 변경으로 구현한다. 실제 코드 수정 요청 시 사용한다.

name: gameplay-evolution-review
description: Use when asked to simulate, evolve, playtest, balance, or evaluate a game/prototype's progression, economy, pacing, player personas, failure routes, exploits, or long-run gameplay experience.

name: gameplay-experience-reviewer
description: Use quando uma ROM, vertical slice ou build jogável SGDK precisar de avaliação independente de game feel, resposta, legibilidade, dificuldade, feedback e experiência observada. Não use para validar apenas contratos de mecânica, código sem execução ou opinião baseada só em documentação.

name: gameplay-experiments
description: Explore Sporefall Station's world in the ECS debugger, compose deterministic scenarios (salvages, set-pieces, emergent-mechanic tests), narrate them on screen with the annotation system, and produce annotated screenshot/video recordings. Use when asked to "try out" gameplay ideas, design multi-stage co-op scenarios, discover emergent mechanics, or make annotated gameplay reels.

name: gameplay-facing-relative-light-aim
description: 用移动决定角色面向，让鼠标只在面向附近的有限角域控制手电方向，并独立开关灯；适用于受限照明控制，不负责武器瞄准、分件姿态或光照阴影算法。

name: gameplay-factory
description: Create or continue gameplay work with continuous primary-agent authorship, tool-owned checkpoints and independent boundary reviews. Resolve project state first; preserve existing CLI and historical formats.

name: gameplay-fantasy-loop-designer
description: 当 $gameplay-design-orchestrator 已完成规范化阶段、且本循环设计阶段 恰好是下一步时使用；或者用于修订已锁定的游戏玩法包的循环层。 不要将其作为自由入口的构思技能使用。

name: gameplay-feature
description: Implement complete SS14 features across ownership, ECS, networking, resources, localization, UI, and tests.

name: gameplay-first
description: A store-page trailer that shows real play from the first seconds: what you do, how it feels, why it is different. Use when the brief kind is gameplay, when it is for a Steam page, or when the request mentions gameplay, a store page, or "何をするゲームか".

name: gameplay-fixed-camera-art-projection
description: 在固定构图相机下，将透视插画贴合简单盒体或圆柱，保留场景深度与遮挡；适用于绘画式环境资产，不用于自由环绕、多面投影或角色朝向相机的 billboard。

name: gameplay-floating-numbers
description: 在瞬时伤害、治疗或得分数字缺少层次、遮挡对象或无法区分事件类型/暴击时设计浮字实例与密集事件布局；共享表现，不混同业务结算或结果总分计数。

name: gameplay-foliage-rustle-response
description: 为穿过或撞入植被的接触音原型接入既有移动速度、强度与方向，以有界的对象级响应替代每次相同的沙沙声；不负责植被形变或断裂倒伏阶段音频。

name: gameplay-framework
description: Implement Unreal's gameplay framework in C++ — GameInstance, AGameModeBase/AGameMode, AGameStateBase/AGameState, APlayerController, APawn/ACharacter, APlayerState, and AHUD — including the server-only spawn/login flow, possession, controller-pawn lifecycle, and which class each piece of logic belongs in. Use when setting up game rules, default pawn/controller classes, player login/spawn/possession, replicated game or player state, match-state machines, respawn logic, or deciding "where does this code live?"

name: gameplay-framework
description: The gameplay framework is the set of base classes Unreal spawns and wires together to run a game. Choosing the *right* class for each piece of logic is the single most important design decision in UE gameplay code.

name: gameplay-gait-step-scheduling
description: 当程序化步态在启动/转向时脚追赶身体，或多脚各自驱动髋部造成冲突时，协调预测迈步、选腿与共享髋运动；两分支按问题选用，不是方向换图、装饰跟随或物理平衡求解器。

name: gameplay-game-design
description: Complete game design document for BlastSimulator2026: satirical open-pit mine management game. Covers core gameplay loop, mining mechanics, economy, events, corruption, world generation, material catalogs, weather, safety, campaign, save system, and win/lose conditions. Use when implementing or modifying any game mechanic or feature.

name: gameplay-gamepad-pitch-limits
description: 当手柄抬头/低头在视角上、下限突然撞停时，为趋近边界的俯仰输入减速，同时让鼠标绕过此边界缓动；保留硬限位、反向离界响应和设备切换，不替代震动、速度 FOV 或基础 up 选择。

name: gameplay-generator
description: Use when the user needs complex gameplay systems (skills, classes, quests, economy, buffs, mana, cooldowns). Triggers on: "add a skill system", "create player classes", "make a quest", "add mana/cooldown", "create a buff/debuff system", or dispatched by mc-mod-master.

name: gameplay-geometric-event-alignment
description: 当切断等离散事件早于或晚于可见物体经过操作边界时，明确几何参照、触发条件与一次性状态，再核对实际事件位置；不负责动画加速或切割网格算法。

name: gameplay-gravity-orientation-cues
description: 当墙面/天花板攀爬或旋转视角让世界向下方向难辨时，设计与真实重力一致的轻量运动线索及覆盖验收；不旋转相机、不改变角色重力，也不把普通落地尘或目标提示当同一任务。

name: gameplay-grid-inventory-placement
description: 为多格背包实现拖放吸附、整块足迹的边界/占用预览、可选直角旋转与有效落位提交；修复只检查锚点、旧格自碰撞和无效拖放丢物，不实现装备、合成、丢弃或堆叠规则。

name: gameplay-harness
description: Use when a game needs an executable driver beside the runtime to inject semantic inputs, replay deterministic tapes, step the project's existing logic clock, and collect inspectable evidence. It does not decide what a session proves, replace game QA, or create a second gameplay clock.

name: gameplay-health-damage-ui
description: 在 HP 变化突兀、损失量难读或低血量提示不清时设计血条平滑、延迟损失段和生命分级；此旧入口保留兼容路由，瞬时浮字与结果总分计数各有独立 owner。

name: gameplay-highlights
description: Use for OpenGGF work compilations, promotional reels, Stageplay or mod showcases, or refreshing highlights after fixes; not individual capture or parity testing.

name: gameplay-hit-recovery
description: 当连续受击使角色难以恢复操作时，评估一段时间内受击阈值脱身及其状态提示；单次受击后的免疫窗口另用独立入口，不将阈值脱身当作无敌。

name: gameplay-hitstop
description: 在命中缺少接触感、或发射/翻牌揭示缺少节奏时设计接触 hit-stop 与非接触表现停顿；不把冰冻状态或全局暂停混为一谈。

name: gameplay-hold-to-multitap
description: 为已支持按住完成的动作增加可选多次轻点入口，逐动作定义推进/取消语义并复用权威执行；保留原按住方式，不把持续防御、跳高或蓄力一律转换为连点。

name: gameplay-hurtbox-tolerance
description: 当攻击或危险障碍擦过角色边缘却命中、项目希望增加空间容差时，设计较小或贴合轮廓的受伤区域并验证命中边界；不把受伤区域等同于世界移动碰撞体，也不提供时间无敌。

name: gameplay-impact-physics-activation
description: 为大量未受扰动的采集道具建立静态待命到受击激活的物理交接，减少不必要的动态模拟；保留首击、碰撞与对象状态，不负责倒伏重心调参或自动休眠系统。

name: gameplay-impact-visuals
description: 改善接触闪光、冲击帧、粒子与碰撞文字，并管理既有战斗残留的寿命和遮挡预算；不把发射残留当命中，贴地余效生成与通用渲染实现不在本入口。

name: gameplay-implementation
description: Implement a gameplay mechanic from agreed rules into an existing engine project, including input, state transitions, lifecycle, feedback, persistence boundaries, and validation. Use for player actions, combat, interactions, inventory, progression, or NPC gameplay behavior.

name: gameplay-implementation
description: Implement gameplay-related tasks in the SENGOKU-DUST-n-FIRE repository safely after repository investigation. Use when implementing features that touch game state, deterministic rules, or the AI-GM boundary. Complements the `.clinerules/` contract and the repo-investigation skill; does not replace them.

name: gameplay-implementation-review
description: Use when a PR or code change exists for a game project and you need to review it for both code quality AND design intent survival. Evolved from /game-code-review — adds Pass 0 checking whether design intent from handoff survived implementation. Not for reviewing design docs (use /game-review), not for feel evaluation (use /feel-pass), not for playability (use /build-playability-review).

name: gameplay-input-normalizer
description: 当 $gameplay-design-orchestrator 已拥有一个游戏设计包的所有权、 且这是必需的首个下游阶段时使用；或者用于仅修订已锁定游戏玩法包的规范化层。 不要将其作为全新游戏构思的常规入口。

name: gameplay-input-remapping-accessibility
description: Audit input remapping and accessibility alternatives for conflict-free actions, device parity, and motor-access needs.

name: gameplay-jump-forgiveness
description: 当角色刚离开平台便无法起跳时，评估 coyote time 的窗口、消费与重置规则；不处理落地前命令缓冲、顶角纠偏或防止离台。

name: gameplay-jump-horizontal-momentum
description: 在一次合法起跳时按已声明方向策略替换或补充水平速度，修复不希望保留的漂移；区分地面/空中跳、来源速度和上限，不改变起跳资格、垂直高度或每帧空中加速。

name: gameplay-jump-input-buffer
description: 当落地前略早按跳被丢弃时，设计有限期的跳跃命令保留、合法时机执行与一次性消费；不同于离地后延长起跳许可，不声称已有可直接移植的输入实现。

name: gameplay-landing-feedback
description: 当落地缺少重量或每帧接地重复播反馈时，绑定真实着地边沿并按高度/接触速度分级；不改跳高、接触物理或落地伤害。

name: gameplay-landing-tumble-recovery
description: 仅在项目明确要求坏落地的玩法后果时，以过快接触且不良接触角触发一次翻倒/布娃娃、短暂失控与持物掉落，再恢复控制和取回资格；不是普通落地特效，不自动添加伤害、敌人感知或噪声规则。

name: gameplay-launch-pad-feedback
description: 当环境跳板弹射缺少弹簧感、起飞与镜头脱节或接触重复触发时，编排跳板压缩、权威弹射、腾空与落地复位；不把视觉拉伸或翻转当跳高、额外跳跃或物理冲量。

name: gameplay-locomotion-contacts
description: 当轮胎等移动部件漏掉路缘或侧面接触时，比较线采样与体积表示的覆盖、稳定性和成本；区分接触物理、网格外观与转向辅助。

name: gameplay-loop
description: Skill for the Gameplay_loop area of TTA. 280 symbols across 15 files.

name: gameplay-loop-pacing
description: Use when combat feels like repetitive kiting (running in circles), objectives stall pacing, or Last Stand timer gameplay feels passive. Focuses on anti-kiting pressure, engagement incentives, and objective pacing while preserving encounter identity.

name: gameplay-loot-pickup
description: 当金币或掉落物的来源、引导和实际领取不清时，区分生成、可拾取、吸附与成功确认；吸附只在既有规则允许时使用，不猜半径、穿障或经济值。

name: gameplay-low-health-damage-reduction
description: 在残血时下一次普通命中立即结束尝试、希望增加有限生存机会时，设计按生命状态缩放伤害的规则与边界测试；不负责固定 1 HP 保命、血条显示或受击无敌窗口。

name: gameplay-mechanic
description: Читай, когда реализуешь игровую механику по её доке — движение, стрельбу, врагов, физику, взаимодействие, всё, что игрок делает или чувствует. Здесь про порядок работы через MCP, устройство кода механики, дешёвый цикл проверки после правки скрипта и про то, что показывать пользователю на приёмку.

name: gameplay-mechanical-interactions
description: 当压板、开关与门体运动/通行状态不一致时，组织触发、机械位移和接地反馈；分段运动、占用和中途反向按明确状态规则处理。

name: gameplay-mechanics
description: Core gameplay mechanics implementation, system interactions, feedback loops, and iterative balance refinement for engaging player experiences.

name: gameplay-mechanics
description: Use when implementing or refining concrete gameplay mechanics, feedback loops, combat, economy, progression, movement, event interactions, or balance iteration.

name: gameplay-mechanism-designer
description: Expand a game-design seed, object, mechanic, image, scene, reference, or rough pitch into structurally distinct gameplay, mechanism chains, repeatable loops, connected systems, and testable prototypes. Use for gameplay ideation, mechanic mutation, reverse-design from visuals, core-loop or system design, prototype planning, and gameplay audits; do not use for purely narrative or visual development that does not require playable rules.

name: gameplay-melee-feedback
description: 为普通近战命中、受击、暴击及重武器重量组合共享反馈；剑轨迹、弹反、踩踏、攻击方向规则和受击脱身使用独立入口，不凭视觉改变判定。

name: gameplay-module
description: Méthode pour ajouter un module de gameplay activable à Meownopoly (système de jeu optionnel type vie, inventaire, monnaie). Utiliser quand l'utilisateur demande de créer/étendre un module de gameplay, un système de jeu activable, ou d'ajouter une section au banc d'essai des modules.

name: gameplay-moment-finder
description: Use when picking moments for a trailer, devlog or short from recorded gameplay: rank candidates from the game's own events and the footage, with a hand-picked fallback when no event fits.

name: gameplay-motion-deformation
description: 在接触、弹跳、按钮反馈或快速出招缺少受力和轮廓时设计 squash/stretch、回弹、视觉后坐与 smear；只管理事件形变，持续跟随、瞄准组合、动作时序和物理接触使用独立入口。

name: gameplay-movement-feedback
description: 当四向/八向移动动画或跑姿与真实运动朝向不一致时校对方向表现；冲刺、落地、跳跃许可和车辆物理使用独立入口，不宣称方向帧增加就降低输入延迟。

name: gameplay-movement-look-decoupling
description: 当观察镜头强制决定角色移动/朝向、妨碍边走边看时，分离移动意图与观察输入，定义移动中及静止时的朝向契约；不是方向帧增加、攻击瞄准、自动转向或相机 up 稳定。

name: gameplay-multiray-object-selection
description: 让解谜或探索游戏的小型交互物更容易选中：在准星附近圆形区域采样多条射线，尊重遮挡并按离准星中心的距离选唯一目标；不转动相机、不提供射击磁吸或自动执行交互。

name: gameplay-navmesh
description: NavMesh and pathfinding specification for BlastSimulator2026: 2D NavGrid derived from VoxelGrid surface, A* with 8-directional movement and octile heuristic, multi-level ramp routing, and dynamic incremental updates after blasts. Use when implementing or modifying agent movement, pathfinding, ramps, or navgrid updates.

name: gameplay-occlusion-reveal

Use when the user asks for a GDD, design doc, one-pager, pitch, feature spec, asset list, scope estimate, art bible, style guide, art or audio direction or accessibility review, or wants a pitch or doc tightened or rewritte…

name: gdd-art-workflow
description: Use when a game project needs durable design documentation or a repeatable AI art pipeline — starting a new game repo, setting up a GDD, deciding where a design decision lives, organizing AI-generated assets (icons, sprites, UI widgets), losing track of which prompt made which image, art drafts piling up untracked, documenting art that already exists, reusing art across projects, or redesigning existing shipped art.

name: gdd-audit
description: Run a design audit by spawning design-auditor, design-integration-checker, and (optionally) design-verifier + design-reflector agents, then printing a consolidated 7-pillar score summary. Use when the user wants to score the current design, retroactively verify a completed cycle, or quickly re-check after a fix. Activates for requests involving scoring an existing design, retroactively reviewing quality, or re-checking after a fix.

name: gdd-author
description: Structure and maintain a living Game Design Document — the single source of truth for the game's design. Use this skill when: (1) creating a GDD from existing design outputs, (2) structuring a modular, navigable document that scales with the project, (3) determining appropriate detail level for different audiences (team, publisher, investor), (4) integrating change tracking from iteration history, (5) generating section templates per domain, (6) ensuring cross-references between sections are maintained. Medium-agnostic — works for digital, tabletop, and hybrid games.

name: gdd-authoring
description: Socratic design partner workflow for authoring Game Design Documents (GDDs) in Godot 4. Guides developers through decision-making on high concepts, core loops, mechanics tuning, systems balance, pacing, and Godot 4 technical architecture.

name: gdd-bandit-reset
description: Confirm-then-reset the per-(agent, bin, delegate) bandit posterior - backs up .design/telemetry/posterior.json to posterior.json.bak, then clears it to a fresh empty envelope. Mutation companion to read-only bandit-status. Use when the posterior is corrupted/unparseable, after a major agent/skill roster change invalidates accumulated arms, or when you deliberately want to rebootstrap adaptive routing from informed priors.

name: gdd-bandit-status
description: Surface read-only per-(agent, bin, delegate) bandit posterior snapshot - alpha/beta/mean/stddev/count/last-used per arm. Phase 27.5 (v1.27.5) diagnostic. Use when investigating 'why did the bandit pick tier X for agent Y?' or when verifying posterior convergence after enabling adaptive_mode: full.

name: gdd-benchmark
description: Harvest and synthesize per-component design benchmarks from 18 design systems and produce canonical component specs at `reference/components/<name>.md`. Use when adding a new component spec, running a benchmark wave, listing corpus coverage, or refreshing a spec after a design-system version bump.

name: gdd-bootstrap-ds
description: Bootstraps a design system for a GREENFIELD project that has none - no Figma, no tokens, no component library. Takes a brand input (primary color + optional secondary + tone tags + target framework) and emits a coherent OKLCH token system (color tints, modular type scale, 4pt/8pt spacing, radius + motion defaults) in 3 variants to pick from, then scaffolds proof components (button/input/card). Use at the start of a brand-new project, or when {{command_prefix}}explore finds no existing design system. Never invents a brand; never overwrites an existing DS.

name: gdd-bootstrap-ds
description: Bootstraps a design system for a GREENFIELD project that has none - no Figma, no tokens, no component library. Takes a brand input (primary color + optional secondary + tone tags + target framework) and emits a coherent OKLCH token system (color tints, modular type scale, 4pt/8pt spacing, radius + motion defaults) in 3 variants to pick from, then scaffolds proof components (button/input/card). Use at the start of a brand-new project, or when /gdd:explore finds no existing design system. Never invents a brand; never overwrites an existing DS.

name: gdd-brainstorming
description: Use for /gdd-dev new-workflow intake before formal HITL, especially when requirements or completion criteria are unclear.

name: gdd-brief
description: Stage 1 of 5 design intake that captures problem statement, audience, constraints, success metrics, and scope into .design/BRIEF.md, and bootstraps .design/STATE.md if missing. Use when starting a new design cycle and before {{command_prefix}}explore. Activates for requests involving capturing a problem statement, defining audience and constraints, or starting a new design brief.

name: gdd-brief
description: Stage 1 of 5 design intake that captures problem statement, audience, constraints, success metrics, and scope into .design/BRIEF.md, and bootstraps .design/STATE.md if missing. Use when starting a new design cycle and before /gdd:explore. Activates for requests involving capturing a problem statement, defining audience and constraints, or starting a new design brief.

name: gdd-brief
description: Fixes what has to pass for one change in a Gate-Driven Development (GDD) project before anyone builds it, with a first estimate of its risk. Loaded by the GDD orchestrator for every change, and when one comes back because it doesn't fit its brief or its color rose. Not for setting up a project, writing checks or building.

name: gdd-budget
description: Forecasts GDD design-cycle spend before the bill arrives. Reads .design/telemetry/costs.jsonl (cost per cycle) + .design/budget.json (the project_cap), runs the pure cost-forecast model via agents/cost-forecaster.md, and projects the next N cycles - surfacing 'at the current rate you'll hit your $X project cap in Y cycles.' Supports --scenario best|typical|worst and --cycles N. Read-only - it forecasts and warns; it never spends, edits budget.json, or halts (the budget-enforcer hook halts). Use to sanity-check spend trajectory before a long run.

name: gdd-build
description: Builds one change through its gates in a Gate-Driven Development (GDD) project, from its brief and its sealed checks. Loaded only by the agent the GDD orchestrator launches to do the work. Not for writing or changing checks, scenarios or the blueprint.

name: gdd-cache-manager
description: Maintains .design/cache-manifest.json for Layer B explicit cache per D-08. Computes deterministic SHA-256 input-hash from (agent-path + sorted-input-file-paths + input-content-hashes). On spawn: lookup key → return cached blob if within TTL, else miss. On completion: write result + TTL. Consulted by hooks/budget-enforcer.ts before every Agent spawn.

name: gdd-check
description: 检查 GDD 能否让 Code Agent 做 V1，输出三态 JSON（PASS/WARNING/BLOCKING）

name: gdd-check
description: Use when a GDD.md for a Phaser.js 2D web game needs a lightweight development-readiness check. Block only issues that would prevent a playable V1; report non-critical gaps as warnings.

name: gdd-check-update
description: Manual plugin-update check. Shows cached state by default; --refresh bypasses the 24h TTL; --dismiss hides the nudge until a newer release ships; --prompt spawns design-update-checker for a richer summary.

name: gdd-checks
description: Writes and seals the cases of a change in Gate-Driven Development (GDD), a test for each scenario of its brief, or sets up a project's standing checks. Loaded only by the agent the GDD orchestrator launches for it, which never builds that change. Not for writing the change itself.

name: gdd-close
description: Closes a change of a Gate-Driven Development (GDD) project once it is in use, by gathering what can be seen against what its brief expected and recording the person's verdict, a yes, a not yet or a no. Loaded by the GDD orchestrator when the person asks to look at a change in use or says whether it helped. Not for a change that hasn't shipped, and never to give the verdict itself.

name: gdd-code-sync
description: Keeps the Game Design Document in design/ and the Luau code in src/ in agreement. Reads the design before coding, updates the pages in the same task, and runs scripts/check-gdd.sh to find drift in remotes, code paths, page names and the PageTree layout. Use for any task that changes game behaviour, adds or removes a system or remote, or asks whether the docs match the code.

name: gdd-compare
description: Compute the delta between the `DESIGN.md` baseline (from explore) and the `DESIGN-VERIFICATION.md` result (from verify), reporting per-category score delta, anti-pattern delta (resolved vs new), must-have pass/fail change, and design drift (regressions without covering tasks in `DESIGN-PLAN.md`). Use after `verify` to measure whether a design pipeline cycle actually improved the design. Writes `.design/COMPARE-REPORT.md`. Activates for requests involving diffing a design baseline against verification output, or a before-after design delta.

name: gdd-complete-cycle
description: Cycle closeout command that marks CYCLES.md entry complete, archives pipeline artifacts to .design/archive/cycle-N/, generates EXPERIENCE.md, rebuilds the search index, and resets STATE.md. Use when a design cycle has shipped and you're ready to start the next one.

name: gdd-completeness-checker
description: 기획 문서(GDD·밸런스 표·경제 원장)가 개발로 넘어갈 자격이 되는지 **기획 게이트**로 검수한다. 근거 없는 추정값, 공란 수치, 숨은 미결, 정의 안 된 성공 지표, 빠진 필수 섹션을 찾아 판정표로 낸다. "기획서 검수해줘", "GDD 빠진 거 없나", "기획 게이트 통과되나", "근거 없는 수치 찾아줘", "미결 정리해줘", "개발 넘겨도 되나" 같은 요청에 사용. 주의: 문서의 **완결성** 검사다. 수치가 재밌는지(balance-sim)·경제가 도는지(econ-sim)· 문체가 자연스러운지(polish-writing)는 다른 축이며 여기서 판정하지 않는다.

name: gdd-completion-check
description: Internal: auto-routed only when Next Action=gdd-completion-check. Verifies completion evidence before done or PR handoff.
